80% finished lower receivers are perfectly legal and require no serial number. Don't even need to go as far as 3D printers. How about a simple press drill is all you need to get a constitutionally legal, unregistered, fully automatic firearm.

First off, 3D printed guns aren't very reliable and are illegal in most areas. Yes, criminals can, in theory, download and print guns. They risk detection in the downloading, and a bigger risk that the plastic gun they printed will explode in their hands. They present a risk to the user, while you just talk glibly about misfires and carrying a dozen of them. Keep in mind carrying a dozen bulky plastic guns is not exactly subtle. The technology's not much further along than old school zip and pipe guns. Yes, criminals will always be able to rig up some sort of firearm that will risk their life.

Laser printers mark pages printed with a yellow microdot that's all but invisible to the naked eye, but can connect a document to the printer it was produced on. Do you really think that the goverment has the pull to accomplish that, but NOT have some sort of tracking and ID system built into 3d printing?

Even if not, It STILL becomes easier to go after those criminals if they have to go through these illegal means to get firearms. Few people can afford 3D printers, much less higher end ones. Same for high end printing materials, it's far less likely that many households will print the guns they want, and more likely that one person in the neighborhood gets a good printer and sets up shop, and then it's far more likely that the law will track them down.

The simple fact of the matter is that criminals will ALWAYS have guns, whether they are legal or not. Criminals will certainly have guns now, with so many loopholes available to get them, whether at gun shows, through strawman sales, or as ghost gun sales. If guns are available legally to citizens there will always be as-of-yet undetected criminals buying and distributing those weapons.

What changes with gun control, then? Many gun advocates would say that it's the 'good people' who won't have guns. But on the flip side, we'll have less trigger-happy criminals if they have less worry that any bystander could be packing a pistol. We'd see far fewer civilian casualties, and leave confronting them to experts who are trained and properly equipped for the risks.

Yes, the counter argument is that an upstanding citizen with a gun could prevent the crime, but in reality it almost never plays out that way. Don't take my word for it, listen to some combat veterans: http://www.patheos.com/blogs/wwjtd/2015/12/combat-veterans-speak-up-to-dispel-the-good-guys-with-guns-narrative/

So if handing out guns to 'good guys' isn't the solution, then the proper approach is to make sure the police have the tools they need when someone misbehaves with a gun, and closing gun registration loopholes would go a long way towards giving those officers critical information.

TLDR: Criminals will always have guns. Encouraging a system that allows multiple forms of secret gun sales only empowers criminals, increases civilian casualties, and makes it more difficult for law enforcement to deal with gun-wielding criminals. So support the laws that let you buy guns publicly, but not in secret.
